$comment: SSS / PhilHealth / Pag-IBIG contribution parameters. These change on statutory schedules; reconcile each block against the current circulars when updating.

value.compensationBase: basic pay plus regular allowances, commissions and other regular pay (all actual remuneration), capped by the ₱35,000 MSC; one-time or liquidated items excluded

legalBasis: RA 11199 (Social Security Act of 2018) Sec 4; 15% is the final scheduled step, in force since 2025
RA 11199 Sec 8(f) and its IRR (compensation: all actual remuneration, including the mandated cost of living allowance)
SSS Circular 2024-006 (employers) and companions 2024-007/008/009/010; the 2025 schedule, still operative for 2026
sss.notes: Re-verified Aug 26, 2026: no 2026 circular supersedes the 2025 schedule and no law suspends the 15%: employer 10% / employee 5%; MSC ₱5,000–₱35,000 in ₱500 steps; the portion above ₱20,000 funds the Mandatory Provident Fund (WISP/MPF). Self-employed, voluntary, and OFW members pay the full 15% themselves (voluntary members have no EC premium). Employer-paid EC: ₱10 below ₱15,000 MSC, ₱30 at or above, confirmed against the 2025 SSS table.

legalBasis: RA 11223 (Universal Health Care Act) Sec 10; 5% final scheduled rate
PhilHealth Advisory 2026-0042 (5% for CY2026 direct contributors; the 2025 reduction proposals did not materialize)
philhealth.notes: Re-verified Aug 26, 2026: 5% of monthly basic salary for CY2026, floor ₱10,000 / ceiling ₱100,000 (premium ₱500–₱5,000), split equally between employer and employee. Self-employed direct contributors pay the full 5% of declared income.

value.employeeShare: premium ÷ 2, rounded half-up to the centavo

legalBasis: Owner default, Oct 7, 2026 (REVIEW.md 4.3): no PhilHealth rule on the odd centavo was found
philhealthShareRounding.notes: When 5% of the salary ends in an odd centavo the two halves cannot be equal. The app gives the employee half rounded half-up to the centavo and the employer the rest, so the shares always add up to the premium (₱10,001 salary: premium ₱500.05 = ₱250.03 employee + ₱250.02 employer). Confirm with PhilHealth which share absorbs the centavo.

legalBasis: HDMF Circular 460; maximum fund salary ₱10,000 effective Feb 2024, still governing in 2026
pagibig.notes: Re-verified Aug 26, 2026: employees earning ≤₱1,500/month contribute 1%, otherwise 2%; employers always 2%; both computed on a fund salary capped at ₱10,000 (max ₱200 + ₱200 = ₱400). Self-employed members contribute on the same schedule based on declared income, shouldering both shares.

pagibigCompensationBase.value: monthly compensation: basic pay plus regular allowances and commissions (one-time or liquidated items excluded), before the ₱10,000 fund-salary cap
legalBasis: Owner default, Oct 7, 2026 (REVIEW.md C05): which pay items count is not confirmed
pagibigCompensationBase.notes: The employee and employer calculators compute Pag-IBIG on the same monthly compensation as SSS (basic pay plus regular allowances and commissions), capped at ₱10,000. Because of the cap this only changes the result for pay of ₱10,000 a month or less (and the 1% / 2% split at ₱1,500). Confirm with Pag-IBIG which pay items count.
